newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope slips out of Vatican on mountain trip.
newsitem.headline: Pope slips out of Vatican on mountain trip.

text.p: Pope John Paul slipped out of the Vatican on Monday for a day in the mountains on his first outing since an appendix operation last month, Italian media reported on Tuesday.

The Pope, his private secretary and a small police escort had travelled by car to the Gran Sasso mountain east of Rome, the highest peak in peninsular Italy, the Rome newspaper Il Messaggero said on Tuesday.
Vatican officials would neither confirm nor deny the reports.
The Polish-born Pope, 76, was an avid mountaineer and hiker in earlier years and has frequently taken unannounced trips from the Vatican into the countryside since his election in 1978.
He has not officially left the Vatican since returning there on October 15 following a 10-day stay at Rome's Gemelli Hospital for surgery to remove his appendix.
Monday was the Roman Catholic feast of Saint Charles Borromeo and the name day of the Pope, born Karol Woytyla.

Though the Pope is still recovering from his operation, he has gradually returned to his formal activities over the past two weeks. Vatican Radio reported on Tuesday that he would resume his weekly general audiences on Wednesday.

He is also scheduled to lead evening prayers on Thursday and a mass at St Peter's on Sunday as part of continuing celebrations of the 50th anniversary of his ordination as a priest on November 1, 1946.
